analysis.summary: Gator Keys makes short investigations into GTA mysteries and Easter eggs: ghosts, Bigfoot, Mount Chiliad, strange buildings and their real-life inspirations, plus a few GTA 6 theories. The thumbnails are one moody game scene with a short line in white handwriting-like bold text and a key word in red: 'SOLVED.', 'finally explained..', 'Welcome to HELL..'.
analysis.niche: GTA mysteries, Easter eggs and real-life history

styleTraits.title: One scene, one mystery
styleTraits.detail: Each thumbnail shows the object of the mystery, close and lit like a horror film: a brain-like lump in a sewer, the Statue of Happiness from below, a sunken wreck, a masked slasher on a dark road.

styleTraits.title: Short phrases with trailing dots
styleTraits.detail: Text is a short white phrase in a heavy rounded font, often ending in two dots: 'finally explained..', 'This Wreck finally makes sense..', 'they have..'. The dots suggest an unfinished thought you want to complete.

styleTraits.title: One red word
styleTraits.detail: Most thumbnails colour a single word red: 'SOLVED.', 'HELL..', 'Wreck', 'Slasher', 'Canon'. It is the word that carries the payoff.

styleTraits.title: Game and real life side by side
styleTraits.detail: Videos about real places split the frame: the GTA IV towers next to the real buildings, or a game character next to a real location. The comparison itself is the hook.

standouts.why: About 990,000 views, 6.2 times the median. The Statue of Happiness seen from below, with a red glow inside, and 'finally explained..' in white. A landmark every GTA player knows plus the promise of an answer may explain the reach.

About 778,000 views, 4.9 times the median. The GTA IV logo, Niko in front of brick towers, the real towers on the right labelled 'real life', and a quote: 'Welcome to HELL..' with 'HELL' in red. Tying a game location to a dark real story probably widened the audience beyond GTA fans.

About 483,000 views, 3.0 times the median. A character with a flashlight finds a strange lump on a dark sewer wall, and 'Sewer brain SOLVED.' sits on the right. The image is weird enough to make people want the explanation.

lessons: Show the mystery object itself, close and dramatically lit, rather than a wide view of the map.
Give your text one coloured word: the one that carries the answer or the fear.
A short phrase with trailing dots can feel like the start of a story.
Game-versus-real-life comparisons can reach people who do not play the game.
On this channel, GTA 6 theory videos sat between 0.4 and 0.6 times the median, while 'solved' mysteries of older games went far higher.
analysis.experiment: On your next explainer, test a thumbnail where only one word of your text is coloured (the answer word) against one where all the text is the same colour.

faq.q: How many subscribers does Gator Keys have?
faq.a: As of 26 October 2026, Gator Keys has about 149K subscribers and only 67 videos. The latest 30 uploads have a median of about 159,500 views, more than the number of subscribers. The biggest in that sample, 'This Is Why There's a HEART Inside The Statue of Happiness...', has about 990,000 views.

faq.q: What does Gator Keys make videos about?
faq.a: GTA lore and mysteries: Easter eggs, ghosts, Bigfoot, Mount Chiliad and hidden places in GTA 5, GTA 4 and San Andreas, the real-life history behind some locations, and a few theories about GTA 6. Most videos run between 4 and 13 minutes.

faq.q: What do Gator Keys' thumbnails look like?
faq.a: One dark, moody game scene showing the mystery object, with a short white phrase in a heavy font, often ending in two dots, and one word in red, such as 'Sewer brain SOLVED.' Real-life videos split the frame between the game and the real place.
